plan:
EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; no experiment has been run)

Objective
Answer: (Q1) Does normalized throughput for 1F1B, 1F1B-I, and ZB-1p improve as microbatch count m increases? (Q2) Does ZB-2p maintain high throughput even at small m? Measurement basis is simulator/analytical makespan only; real GPU execution is out of scope by design (scope boundary, not a limitation).

1. System under study (design basis)
The published Zero-Bubble pipeline-parallelism reference implementation structure: schedule generators for 1F1B, 1F1B-interleaved (1F1B-I), ZB-1p, ZB-2p; a deterministic event-driven timing simulator producing per-device timelines and step makespan from a cost model; a schedule validator; and a bench-style sweep harness. No code exists in the masked workspace, so the design is specified against this structure and remains valid for any faithful instantiation (repo simulator primary; closed-form schedules as cross-check/fallback).

2. Configuration matrix (fixed controls; p is NOT swept)
- Methods: 1F1B (v=1), 1F1B-I (v=2), ZB-1p (v=1), ZB-2p (v=2).
- Pipeline stages p ∈ {4, 8} — two separate fixed experiments.
- Interleaving chunks v = 2 for all interleaved methods. Equal-v comparison of 1F1B-I vs ZB-2p isolates the effect of input-interleaved immediate-forward recomputation from plain chunked interleaving.
- Cost models (both reported): CM1 unit-cost f=b=w=1 (primary); CM2 b=2f with w treated per repo convention (robustness). Same cost model applied identically to all methods; ZB-2p's extra forward-recompute ops are charged as real forward work in the makespan (validity check V4).
- Communication: only what the repo cost model includes; no additional network modeling.

3. Sweep grid (independent variable m)
- Primary: contiguous m = 1..4p (m=1..16 for p=4; m=1..32 for p=8) — dense coverage of the small-m regime central to Q2.
- Extended: powers-of-two-style grid {1,2,4,8,16,32,48,64,96,128} merged with the contiguous grid; m=128 is the "large-m asymptote" reference point for criterion (a).
- Total cells: 2 p-values × 2 cost models × 4 methods × ≤ ~48 m-values ≈ 768 makespan evaluations (deduped).

4. Metrics (dependent variables)
- Makespan T(method, m, p, v, CM): simulated single training-step time, in the repo's abstract time units.
- Ideal work per step W_id = m·(f + b) (per microbatch required non-recompute compute, per-unit-device; w handled per CM convention, identical across methods). Normalized throughput N = W_id / T ∈ (0,1], equal to 1 − bubble ratio; primary comparison metric, comparable across m.
- Raw throughput R = m / T (microbatches per time unit) reported as secondary.
- Bubble ratio B = 1 − N reported for figure parity with the paper.
- m90: smallest m with N(m) ≥ 0.90·N(128) (efficiency-at-low-m statistic).

5. Feasibility rules (undefined points)
- Run the repo's schedule generator/validator for every (method, m); any rejection (e.g., divisibility or minimum-m constraints for ZB-1p/ZB-2p in a given version) is recorded in a per-method feasible-domain table D_method, never silently skipped.
- Monotonicity is assessed only over each method's feasible domain; the feasible-domain caveat is reported next to every Q1 verdict (e.g., "1F1B improves over all m≥1; ZB-1p improves over its feasible m ∈ D_ZB1p").

6. Analysis plan and decision criteria
Q1 (per method ∈ {1F1B, 1F1B-I, ZB-1p}, per p, per CM, over feasible domain):
- (i) Non-decreasing: N(m_{i+1}) ≥ N(m_i) − ε for all consecutive feasible points, ε = 1e-9 (deterministic simulator).
- (ii) Substantial strict increase: N(m_max) − N(min feasible m) ≥ 0.05 absolute and strictly increasing across ≥ 50% of consecutive feasible pairs.
- (iii) Saturation: |N(128) − N(64)| ≤ 0.02 (curve flattens toward the zero-bubble bound).
- (iv) Spearman ρ(m, N) ≥ +0.95 over feasible domain.
- (v) Marginal-gain statistic: Δ = N(4p) − N(p), reported per method/p (expected: ZB-1p starts higher than 1F1B at m=p; similar Δ at large m).
Verdict "improves as m increases" iff (i)–(iv) hold; (v) is descriptive.

Q2 (ZB-2p), criteria reported separately, not folded:
- (a) Self-referential: N_ZB2p(m) ≥ 0.90·N_ZB2p(128) for all feasible m ≤ p.
- (b) Competitive ceiling: N_ZB2p(m) ≥ max{N_1F1B(128), N_1F1B-I(128), N_ZB1p(128)} for all feasible m ≤ p.
Report a per-(p)×(CM) pass/fail table for (a) and (b) independently; (b) is the stronger claim. Secondary: ZB-2p m90 vs the other methods' m90.

7. Validity checks (named deliverables)
- V1 Validator-on-every-schedule: 100% of accepted schedules pass the repo validator; rejects logged.
- V2 Determinism: each cell run twice; makespans must be bit-identical (event-driven simulator, no stochastic components).
- V3 Closed-form cross-checks (required): simulated 1F1B bubble ratio within 1e-6 of (p−1)/(m+p−1); 1F1B-I bubble ratio matches the interleaved closed form scaled by v; ZB-2p simulated bubbles fall in the paper's near-zero, m-independent/rapidly-decaying bubble class (near-flat high N even for m ≤ p).
- V4 Recompute-cost accounting (named deliverable): artifact demonstrating that every ZB-2p input-forward recompute op appears as a forward-duration interval on the device timeline inside the makespan — verified by counting recompute ops in the generated schedule and matching the simulated busy-time increment; ensures the equal-v ZB-2p vs 1F1B-I comparison charges ZB-2p's extra work.

8. Output artifacts → sub-question checklist
- A1: N-vs-m curve panel (per p, per CM, all 4 methods) → Q1 and Q2.
- A2: Q1 verdict table (per method × p × CM: checks i–iv, ρ, Δ, feasible domain) → Q1.
- A3: Q2 pass/fail table for criteria (a) and (b) separately (per p × CM), plus m90 table → Q2.
- A4: Feasible-domain / infeasibility table D_method → caveat reporting for Q1 and Q2.
- A5: Validity report V1–V4 → internal validity of all claims.
- A6: Raw-throughput R and bubble-ratio B appendix → figure parity with the paper.

9. Feasibility section (cost and failure modes)
- Runtime: makespans come from closed-form schedules or a discrete-event simulator over ≤ 4×128×2 operator slots per device; the entire ≤768-cell sweep is seconds of CPU. A closed-form arithmetic probe of the full grid executed during design (304 evaluations) took 0.0001 s, confirming trivial compute cost; a single core suffices.
- What could fail: (F1) ZB-1p/ZB-2p generators reject some m — handled by §5 feasible-domain rules; report which m and which constraint fired. (F2) A repo variant's w-convention differs from CM2 — handled by applying the repo's own convention uniformly and documenting it; CM1 is convention-free. (F3) Simulator lacks explicit comm model — comm is then out of scope and stated so; conclusions limited to compute-bubble effects. (F4) If the exact repo build is unavailable, run the design on closed-form schedule constructions plus the paper's bubble-ratio formulas; V3 becomes the primary evidence path. None threaten answerability of Q1/Q2, only caveat granularity.
- Scope boundary (fixed): no real execution, no GPU, no memory-capacity feasibility analysis, no failure/recovery behavior; ZB-2p memory-neutrality is an analytical property outside this experiment.

context.question: Does the throughput for methods 1F1B, 1F1B-I, and ZB-1p improve as the number of microbatches increases, while ZB-2p maintains high throughput even with fewer microbatches? (Note: These methods are implemented as part of the zero bubble pipeline parallelism strategies in this repository, which aim to reduce pipeline bubbles and maintain high throughput.)
